flags.item: Two build scripts write into the same output directory, so one session's rebuild silently mutates another session's published data
flags.detail: pipeline/build_site_data.py (session 0a016df8) has OUT = f'{ROOT}/site/data' at line 6, which is the data directory of the site owned by session 7c532e8c. Running it during this session's verification modified site/data/injuries.json, picks.json, props.json and schedule.json and added 6 files that were not in the committed tree. These were reverted with git checkout, so main is unaffected, but any CI run or any future session that rebuilds edge/ will overwrite 7c532e8c's site data with different content.
flags.action_needed: Owner to decide: retarget pipeline/build_site_data.py to edge/data only, or merge the two sites so there is one owner of site/data. Do not run pipeline/build_site_data.py until decided.

flags.item: One of the two 174-game result sets cites Basketball-Reference, which is not an official NBA source
flags.detail: The header of data/raw/results_2026-27_october.csv names https://www.basketball-reference.com/... as its source. The user rule for this project is that every row must cite an official site. The same 174 games were re-verified this session against the official NBA.com pages and against official team records, and the scores agree, so the values are not in doubt - but the citation for those rows is not an official one. The October file also documents an 8-column format ('date, start_ET, away_team, ...') while each row actually holds 5 fields, so the header comment does not describe the file.
flags.action_needed: Treat data/origin/games.csv (officially sourced) as canonical, which this build does. Either re-cite the edge capture at an NBA.com URL or mark those rows cross-check-only.

flags.item: Six independent dashboards are published side by side with five incompatible ID namespaces
flags.detail: docs/ (f879620b), site/ (7c532e8c), research/ (9ed6085f), lab/ (5697caaf), edge/ (0a016df8) and origin/ (e22a2831) each publish their own landing page, their own flags and their own injury snapshot. Flags F01, SG-01, Q-01 etc. mean different things in each tree, so a reader comparing two pages can reach opposite conclusions from identical-looking IDs. The root page cannot be used as a decision document because it is not clear which numbers are current.
flags.action_needed: This round publishes dash/ as the single entry point and the root page now routes there. Owner decision needed on whether the six trees are archived read-only (recommended) or consolidated further.

flags.item: The three engines' headline RMSE figures are not comparable, and two of them quote different correlations for the same quantity
flags.detail: On the spread model: origin reports 16.18 vs baseline 17.30 over 114 out-of-sample games; edge reports 14.95 for its consensus model over 138 games with 'baseline' defined as the population standard deviation of all margins in the full log; this build reports 15.48 vs 16.73 over the same 114 games as origin. Different windows and different baseline definitions, not different models. On spread/total residual correlation origin publishes r=+0.091, edge publishes -0.018 and this build measures +0.023 - all three are inside zero's interval, so they agree statistically but not numerically, and none of them is a usable input to a parlay price.
flags.action_needed: Publish one headline metric per model, computed on one agreed window and one agreed baseline. Owner to choose the window (this build uses 60-game burn-in to match origin) and the baseline definition.

flags.item: No market price exists in the repository, so no strategy can be scored on profit - only on self-consistency
flags.detail: Every ROI figure in this repository, including this build's, is computed against our own originated line at an assumed -110. That measures whether the signal contradicts our own model; it cannot measure whether we beat a book. A moneyline graded against our own fair price is exactly zero by construction, so STR-13 is published with a null result and is marked not gradable.
flags.action_needed: Owner decision: whether licensed or clearly-labelled third-party closing prices may be used for comparison only. Without that decision, no pick page can show edge, and the reward rule for the strategy leaderboard cannot be computed.

flags.item: Same-slate cross-game correlation is left unestimated rather than assumed to be zero
flags.detail: Multi-game parlays depend on whether games on the same date share a forecast error. With 114 out-of-sample games the within-date pairs are too few for an interval worth quoting, so the value is blank in the correlation table. Assuming 0 here is what makes a 4-leg parlay look affordable.
flags.action_needed: Needs roughly 4-6 weeks of games at this slate size, or a published estimate the owner accepts as a prior.

flags.item: Player props and player-level correlations remain blocked: only the 31 highest-minute players in the league have official minutes in the repository
flags.detail: data/origin/players_top_minutes.csv holds 31 rows. Every 'minutes at risk' figure is therefore a floor, not an estimate: of the 4 Out/Doubtful designations on the 11/14 slate that could be matched, 1 (Anthony Edwards, 33.7 mpg) is quantified and 3 are not. No player game logs, so no per-player scoring distribution, so prop lines cannot be originated at all - and no player points-vs-minutes correlation can be measured.
flags.action_needed: Carried forward from CR-O1 and CR-O2 (still open): capture the full official minutes table and dated player box scores. Until then the prop page must stay blank.

flags.item: Game-flow analysis is schedule-and-result based only; in-game states are not available
flags.detail: Lead changes, halftime margins, fourth-quarter usage and four-factor splits would need play-by-play and per-game box scores. Neither is in the repository and stats.nba.com was not reachable from this workspace, so those fields are published as null instead of being proxied by something else. What is published (rest days, back-to-backs, OT rate, margin distribution, home performance) is computed from the 174 verified results.
flags.action_needed: Owner to decide whether play-by-play acquisition is in scope.

flags.item: Availability moves fast enough that a same-evening snapshot was already wrong on a star player
flags.detail: Between the 11/13 05:00 PM and 07:30 PM reports: Klay Thompson Probable to Out, Pelle Larsson Doubtful to Out, Norman Powell Questionable to Available with no reason printed, and Anthony Edwards appears as Out for 11/14 in the later captures while the 05:00 PM capture carries only 2 rows for that game. All three of the 05:00 PM vs 05:15 PM status differences were checked against both PDFs and are genuine report updates, not transcription errors - two prior sessions had this flagged as a possible transcription dispute.
flags.action_needed: No action on the data; the process must re-pull the newest report at pick time and stamp it. This build prices 11/14 from the 07:30 PM report, which is the newest that exists.

flags.item: Half of the teams in the live window had not filed a designation at the newest available report
flags.detail: For the five games on 11/14, 10 teams are scheduled and 5 of them (NOP, CLE, MEM, CHI, MIA) print 'NOT YET SUBMITTED' with no player rows. For those teams the availability input is unknown, not 'healthy'. Any model that treats a missing row as no absence will systematically understate injury impact.
flags.action_needed: Confirm the pick engine distinguishes 'no rows' from 'all available' (this build does: report_status is carried on every line) and decide whether to suppress lines for games where either team has not filed.

flags.item: The 11/13 slate was in progress while this build ran, so results and pricing windows had to be split
flags.detail: At retrieval (2026-11-14T00:52Z, i.e. 11/13 19:52 ET) NYK-IND and MIL-ORL were in the first quarter and seven 11/13 games were pregame. The results set therefore stops at 11/12 and pricing starts at 11/14, leaving 11/13 unpriced and ungraded.
flags.action_needed: None for the owner; recorded so that the gap in the slate is not read as missing work. A nightly run after the last tip removes it.

flags.item: Two standing legal blockers from earlier sessions are still open and still bind publication
flags.detail: NBA.com Terms of Use restrict reproduction and use of NBA Statistics in connection with gambling (flagged as 7C-F-01), and offering online sports betting to Dutch consumers requires a Kansspelautoriteit licence (7C-F-02). Both were recorded by prior sessions against the official pages; this session did not re-read them and is not qualified to clear them.
flags.action_needed: Counsel opinion before any pick page is used for staking decisions or promoted. Publishing analysis under a research label is the current posture and is not the same as being cleared.

flags.item: Pages still serves the whole repository from main with the legacy build type
flags.detail: Because the source is 'main /' rather than a workflow artifact, every per-session tree, the scratch CSVs and data/ are all publicly reachable. Three prior sessions each tried to switch the Pages source and each got HTTP 403 from the API with the sandbox token.
flags.action_needed: Owner to switch Pages to the Actions artifact, or accept the exposure deliberately. This is a settings change, not a code change.

flags.item: A 3-day window cannot cover a full NBA slate cycle
flags.detail: The brief caps the horizon at 3 days in advance. On 11/15 there are 9 games and on 11/16 there are 8, but 11/17 has 5 and 11/18 has 12 (per the official month grid), so a 3-day cap skips double-digit slates that a back-to-back-aware model would want to see in advance.
flags.action_needed: Owner to confirm whether 3 days is a hard product rule or a default that can be widened per strategy.

flags.item: The reward rule cannot be computed as specified
flags.detail: A leaderboard that pays the top strategies needs a score. Profit is unavailable (E-F-05) and no strategy clears the sample gate (largest gradable sample is 18 bets against a floor of 100), so the only rankable quantity today is forecast quality against actual outcomes - which is what this build publishes - and it is not the same thing as making money.
flags.action_needed: Owner to choose the scoreboard metric explicitly: forecast skill (available now) or realised PnL (needs prices).

questions.question: May third-party closing prices be stored in this repository for comparison, if they are never copied into our published line?
questions.why_it_matters: It decides whether the leaderboard can ever score profit instead of self-consistency (E-F-05).
questions.what_we_have: Nothing. There are no odds in the repo, and no official NBA odds table was reachable.
questions.what_we_lack: A written decision, and a dated price source with terms.

questions.question: Who captures full official minutes and dated player box scores, and is that acquisition in scope?
questions.why_it_matters: Without it, prop lines, prop combos and player-level correlations stay impossible (E-F-07), and injury minutes impact remains a floor.
questions.what_we_have: 31 players' season MPG, cross-checked against the top of the official table.
questions.what_we_lack: The full minutes table (roughly 465 rows) and per-game player logs.
questions.owner_action: Approve the capture, or descope props from the roadmap.

questions.question: What stake does a strategy get when it clears the gates, and who decides it?
questions.why_it_matters: The gates can be passed and still produce an unusable process if bet sizing, max exposure and correlation limits are undefined.
questions.what_we_have: Gate definitions and a measured same-game parlay dependence factor.
questions.what_we_lack: Bankroll, unit size, per-slate exposure cap, and a rule for correlated legs.
questions.owner_action: State a staking policy; the site will publish it next to the picks.

questions.question: Should a line be suppressed when a team has not filed, or published with an 'unknown availability' badge?
questions.why_it_matters: 5 of 10 teams in the live window had not filed (E-F-10). The two choices give different pick counts on the same night.
questions.what_we_have: report_status carried on every originated line, so the build can do either.

questions.question: Which of the two report-stamps do we price from - the 5:00 p.m. day-before report, or the newest file that exists at run time?
questions.why_it_matters: Statuses changed on four players between 5:00 p.m. and 7:30 p.m. on 11/13 (E-F-09). Pricing from a fixed stamp is reproducible; pricing from the newest is more correct and less reproducible.
questions.what_we_have: Both stamps in the repository, transcribed and diffed.
questions.owner_action: Newest-at-run-time (recommended, store the stamp) / Fixed 5 p.m. stamp

questions.question: Are the six existing site trees archived or merged into one?
questions.why_it_matters: Today a reader can find six different 'current' numbers (E-F-03). Consolidation is the single highest-value change to decision quality.
questions.what_we_have: dash/ as a single entry point with a per-tree archive index; nothing deleted.
questions.what_we_lack: Approval to mark the old trees superseded in their own headers (their files are owned by other sessions).
questions.owner_action: Archive as-is / Add a superseded banner / Merge fully

questions.question: Should the build fail CI when the published tables go stale?
questions.why_it_matters: Every table here is dated 2026-11-13. A dashboard that keeps looking live after its data ages is worse than no dashboard.
questions.what_we_have: as_of fields in data/integration/model.json and a checker that reads them.
questions.what_we_lack: A scheduled workflow that re-runs the capture and fails on age.
questions.owner_action: Approve a daily workflow with a staleness threshold of 24 hours

questions.question: Is a 100-bet minimum the right sample floor, given a 174-game season start?
questions.why_it_matters: At n=100 and 55% hit rate the interval is 45-64%: the floor is enough to reject luck-ish performance, not enough to size edge. With 8 strategies tested, no realistic December sample clears everything.
questions.what_we_have: Wilson intervals, permutation tests and BH-FDR implemented and unit-tested.
questions.what_we_lack: Owner's risk appetite, or a decision to run the leaderboard across a whole season.

questions.question: May the same-game parlay legs be priced as independent, given a measured dependence ratio of 1.06 on 114 games?
questions.why_it_matters: It sets whether a 2-leg same-game parlay is being under- or over-valued by the market convention.
questions.what_we_have: The measured ratio and its interval are published on the correlations page; the point estimate is small and its interval includes 1.
questions.what_we_lack: More games. Do not build a pricing rule on this alone.

questions.question: Has Dutch counsel cleared publishing model output that names a side, even under a research label?
questions.why_it_matters: The standing blockers (E-F-12) were recorded against official pages by earlier sessions and were never cleared; the picks page is the item most likely to need that clearance.
questions.what_we_have: Two prior sessions' reading of the NBA terms and the Ksa licence page.
questions.owner_action: Obtain counsel opinion before the pick page is shared beyond this project

suggestions.suggestion: Make one page the source of truth and mark everything else an archive
suggestions.detail: dash/ now renders every current number from one model artefact, and the root page points at it. The six per-session trees stay online and untouched for history, but a 'superseded by dash/' banner should be added to each of their headers by their owners so nobody reads an old injury snapshot as live.
suggestions.decision_needed: Approve the banner and freeze the six trees read-only.

suggestions.suggestion: Retarget pipeline/build_site_data.py so no build writes into another session's directory
suggestions.detail: It writes into site/data (E-F-01). This round had to revert it. The fix is a one-line path change plus a CI assertion that a build only writes inside its own output tree.
suggestions.decision_needed: Approve the path change, or move both sites onto one generator.

suggestions.suggestion: Add a decision column to the suggestions page that writes back to COORDINATION.md
suggestions.detail: Suggestions are currently a read-only list, so approving one requires editing a file by hand. A form cannot persist on GitHub Pages; a 'copy this line into COORDINATION.md' button plus a machine-readable decision block at the top of the page gets 90% of the benefit with no backend.
suggestions.decision_needed: Approve the pattern, or accept a small JSON file committed by hand.

suggestions.suggestion: Run the capture nightly after the last tip, and stamp every table with the report time
suggestions.detail: Availability moved on four players inside 2.5 hours on 11/13 (E-F-09) and half the window had not filed (E-F-10). A dashboard that shows yesterday's 5 p.m. report as 'injuries' is actively misleading; every table here now carries its stamp.
suggestions.decision_needed: Approve a scheduled workflow, or keep manual runs and accept staleness.

suggestions.suggestion: Publish one agreed evaluation window and baseline, then re-score all three engines against it
suggestions.detail: Three engines currently quote incomparable RMSEs and three different correlation values for one quantity (E-F-04). Re-scoring origin/, edge/ and this build on the same 114 games with the same baseline turns a confusing set of claims into an actual leaderboard of models.
suggestions.decision_needed: Adopt the 60-game burn-in and the expanding-mean baseline as the house standard.

suggestions.suggestion: Score strategies on forecast calibration (Brier + reliability), not only on hit rate
suggestions.detail: A pick page that says 'over 229.0' is a claim about a distribution. Calibration rewards honest probabilities; hit rate alone can be gamed by only betting near-50/50 games. Edge already publishes reliability buckets, so there is a working example in-repo.
suggestions.decision_needed: Adopt Brier + reliability as the primary leaderboard metric, keep hit rate secondary.

suggestions.suggestion: Add a gate that blocks any correlated multi-leg ticket until cross-game dependence is measured
suggestions.detail: The cross-game correlation is deliberately blank (E-F-06). Without a rule, a parlays page will price 4 legs as independent by default and the error compounds multiplicatively.
suggestions.decision_needed: Add gate E-G10 'parlay legs must be provably independent or the ticket is blocked'.

suggestions.suggestion: Show the interval next to every number, and grey out any pick whose interval straddles the line
suggestions.detail: Our own 95% interval on a projected margin is about plus or minus 31 points, which means most single games are not decidable. Displaying the interval makes 'no bet' a visible, default outcome rather than a failure to find a pick.

suggestions.suggestion: Widen the horizon to 5 days for schedule-aware signals, keeping 3 days for priced picks
suggestions.detail: Rest and back-to-back value is visible earlier than a price is. The 3-day cap throws away the part of the edge that is knowable in advance (E-F-14).
suggestions.decision_needed: Split the horizon by signal family, or keep one horizon.

suggestions.suggestion: Require a written pre-registration per strategy before it can enter the leaderboard
suggestions.detail: Twelve strategies were tried here; two look good on 18 and 30 bets and none survives the sample floor. Pre-registering the rule, the sample floor and the metric before results exist is what makes a p-value on a leaderboard mean anything.
suggestions.decision_needed: Adopt pre-registration as a submission requirement.

suggestions.suggestion: Switch Pages to the workflow artifact so only the built site is public
suggestions.detail: Three sessions hit HTTP 403 with the sandbox token (E-F-13); this needs an owner with repo settings access. Until then the whole repository, including scratch data, is published.
suggestions.decision_needed: Owner to change the Pages source in settings.

suggestions.suggestion: Keep the row-level source link requirement as a hard build failure, and extend it to numeric values
suggestions.detail: The checker here fails if a table row has no official source or if a blank is unflagged. Extending it to assert that each published number appears in the artefact that produced it would catch the class of error that E-F-01 and E-F-04 both come from.
